name: London School of Economics and Political Science

settingEvidence.evidence: Located in the heart of London, LSE provides one of the most exciting places in the world to study for your philosophy degree.

fees.text: £10,050 per year for Home (UK) students starting in 2027/28. LSE says the Home fee is set in line with the UK Government's maximum fee and may increase in later years if that maximum changes.

source.evidence: This is the tuition fee for Home students starting in 2027/28.

livingCosts.text: LSE estimates you should allow at least £1,550 a month for all living expenses in London (accommodation, travel, food, laundry, study costs and other personal costs). It varies with your lifestyle. The page does not say which academic year the estimate is for.

source.evidence: We estimate that you should allow for at least £1,550 per month for all living expenses, including accommodation, travel, food, laundry, study costs, and other personal expenses.

openDays.text: Next undergraduate Open Day: April 2027 (exact date not announced yet). LSE holds two a year, in April and July.

source.evidence: Our next Open Day will take place in April 2027. More details will appear here closer to the time.

contextual.summary: If you have Home fee status and meet any one of LSE's contextual flags (care-experienced, free school meals in the last six years, a lowest-participation home area, or an LSE or Sutton Trust access programme), you may be considered for a contextual offer one or two grades lower.
contextual.typicalReduction: One or two grades lower than the standard entry requirements, depending on the degree programme. Any Maths requirement must still be met.

criteria.detail: You are a care-experienced student: you have spent time living with foster carers under local authority care, in residential care (for example a children's home), looked after at home under a supervision order, or in kinship care with relatives or friends (officially or informally).
You have been eligible for free school meals (FSM) within the previous six years. Tick the FSM question on UCAS and ask your teacher to confirm it in their reference.
Your home postcode is in TUNDRA Quintile 1 (the 20% lowest for university participation) if you live in England. If you live in another UK nation LSE uses the POLAR4 dataset instead.

You have completed an intensive LSE widening participation programme (LSE Springboard, LSE Thrive, LSE Pathways to Law or LSE Pathways to Banking and Finance) or any Sutton Trust Pathways programme at a UK university (Engineering, Medicine, Law, Banking and Finance or Consulting).

contextual.rulesText: You may be eligible for a contextual offer if you have Home fee status and meet one or more of the criteria. LSE flags the information automatically from your UCAS form. Contextual offer grades are listed on each programme page. Having a contextual flag does not guarantee an offer, and LSE also uses other contextual information for extra consideration rather than a lower offer.

source.evidence: You may be eligible for a contextual offer if you have Home fee status and meet one or more of the criteria below.

programmes.name: LSE Springboard
programmes.provider: London School of Economics and Political Science
programmes.summary: Free 10-month access programme (January to November 2027) for Year 12 students outside London and the South East, with campus visits, online academic tutorials and application support; finishing it lets you be considered for a contextual offer at LSE.
programmes.whoCanApply: Year 12 students who have always attended a UK state school or college, live in England or Wales outside London and the South East, have at least grade 6 in GCSE English Language and Maths and mostly grades 7-9 at GCSE, and are on track for LSE's contextual offer grades.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Essential: in Year 12; always attended a UK state (non-fee-paying) school or college; live in a region of England or Wales that is not London or the South East; interested in applying to LSE; able to commit to all activities from January to November 2027; able to travel to LSE and back in a day (no more than about three hours each way); at least grade 6 in GCSE English Language and Maths; a strong set of GCSEs with the majority at 7, 8 and 9; on track for at least the contextual offer grades for your chosen LSE programme (including any required A-level subjects). Applications are then reviewed against additional criteria in priority order (care-experienced; low higher-education participation area, TUNDRA quintile 1 or 2; free school meals; estranged from both parents; first generation to go to university) and extenuating circumstances.
benefits: Free: LSE pays for all activities and for travel to and from campus
Finishing the programme and applying to LSE means you can be considered for a contextual offer (not guaranteed)
Three campus visits, four academic tutorials with The Brilliant Club, admissions and personal statement support

programmes.name: LSE Pathways to Banking and Finance
programmes.provider: London School of Economics and Political Science
programmes.summary: Free 18-month programme for Year 12 state-school students within about 90 minutes of LSE (run with the Sutton Trust): finance taster lectures, mentoring, work experience and a funded summer residential at the University of Warwick; you must be taking A-level or IB Higher Level Maths.
programmes.whoCanApply: Year 12 students who have always attended a state-funded, non-fee-paying school or college and live within about 90 minutes of LSE, with at least five GCSEs at grades 9-6 (including English Language and Maths, two of them at 9-7), who are studying Maths at A-level or IB Higher Level and at least two traditional academic subjects.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Mandatory: always attended a state-funded, non-fee-paying school or college; studying in Year 12; live within reasonable commuting distance of LSE (up to 90 minutes). Academic: at least five GCSEs at grades 9-6 (or equivalent) including English Language and Maths, with at least two at 9-7; studying A-level or IB Higher Level Mathematics; studying at least two full A-levels or IB Higher Levels in traditional academic subjects. Additional criteria considered: first generation in your family to go to university; free school meals at secondary school; attend a school or college with a below-average A-level or Higher point score or low progression to higher education; live in a neighbourhood with a low rate of progression to higher education or high socio-economic deprivation; looked after or in care. If you are (or have been) in care you only need to meet the mandatory and academic requirements.
benefits: Free: travel expenses for in-person events can be claimed back, and the National Conference at Warwick is fully funded
Completing it gives your LSE application additional consideration and you may be considered for a contextual offer (not guaranteed)
Finance taster lectures, mentoring by current LSE students, employer insight events and work experience placements (places are limited)

notes: No 2028-entry course pages yet (checked 2026-10-21): the newest LSE course pages are for 2027 entry (academic year 2027/28, start 27 September 2027), so courses use 2027 entry. BSc Geography with Economics only shows 2026-entry requirements (2027 entry 'still subject to confirmation').

TMUA (2027 entry): mandatory for BSc Economics and BSc Econometrics and Mathematical Economics; recommended but not mandatory for Mathematics and Economics and Economics and Data Science (and other maths programmes). Not used for Politics and Economics, PPE, Geography with Economics or Finance.

LSE says it received approximately 34,000 applications for roughly 1,900 places in 2026 (whole university, not per course). Per-course application, intake and ratio figures (labelled 2025) are on most programme pages and are recorded under each course's competition.
LSE does not interview candidates. Its UCAS deadline for September 2027 entry is 13 January 2027 at 18:00.

Contextual offers are one or two grades lower than the standard offer, and any Maths requirement must still be met. Completing LSE Pathways to Law or any Sutton Trust Pathways programme (Engineering, Medicine, Law, Banking and Finance, Consulting) also counts as a contextual flag; LSE Pathways to Law is not listed under programmes because it is a law programme.
LSE halls: rates start from £100 a week for a shared self-catered room (accommodation prices page). Private housing in London starts at about £650 a month (London on a budget page).

Other LSE degrees with Economics exist but are not recorded here: Accounting and Finance, Economics and Economic History, Mathematics with Economics, Philosophy and Economics, Management and Economic History.
